inventedEvidence.evidence: 'Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged' - the customer reported no tripped breaker and never reset anything.

rationale: The assistant reached the right destination, an appliance engineer, and named no part. But the final message is a stop-use warning built on a trip that never happened: the customer found no tripped breaker and reset nothing. It also tells them to leave the hob unplugged although three zones work normally, and it never asked for the full model number or explained the likely element-versus-board cause. The earlier turns were clumsy too: 'Now try switching a zone on' came before the customer had said anything to act on, and the first message gave no real diagnostic framing.
